claims.title: Player-local client traffic may expose player data if local transport protection is absent
claims.description: `flow:entity:player>process:game-client>launch-and-play` has `encryption_in_transit: unknown` while connecting `entity:player`, which holds `pii`, to `process:game-client` on hardware the operator does not control. If this local path is IPC or another observable channel without suitable local protection, malware or another local user controlling the player's machine can intercept player input and game output. This is conditional on the unverified transport attribute and on what data the local channel carries; it does not assert that encryption is absent. Second-order, captured local game data can enable account-targeted social engineering or observation of the affected player's activity.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first control or access the player's local machine or local execution environment. Impact is low because the modeled path is limited to one player's own input and output, although `entity:player` is tagged `pii`.

mitigations.summary: Specify and protect the local client channel
mitigations.detail: Establish whether this `local` path is in-process or IPC; where it is IPC, apply OS access controls and authenticated local endpoints, and avoid placing sensitive account data in unprotected local messages.

claims.title: Unverified encryption may expose gameplay state on the player-to-game-server path
claims.description: `flow:process:game-client>process:game-server>gameplay-traffic` crosses from `boundary:player-local-machine` to `boundary:production-network` and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If transport protection is absent or ineffective, an attacker able to observe the player-facing TCP 1235 path can intercept gameplay actions and state updates exchanged with `process:game-server`. The game server holds `business-critical-data`; captured state can reveal match activity and provide intelligence for targeting players or manipulating later game interactions. This is conditional on the unverified encryption state, not an assertion that the TCP flow is plaintext.

quotes.text: It talks to the lobby on TCP 1234 for matchmaking, and once a match starts it talks directly to the game servers on TCP 1235.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because this is a player-network-to-production boundary crossing with an unverified transport control, but interception still requires an on-path position. Impact is medium because the flow reaches `process:game-server`, which holds `business-critical-data`, and exposes live match state.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated TLS for gameplay traffic
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:game-client>process:game-server>gameplay-traffic` to TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation; use mutually authenticated credentials where the client identity design permits it.

mitigations.summary: Minimize sensitive state in each message
mitigations.detail: Avoid transmitting unnecessary player identifiers or durable account information in gameplay state updates.

claims.title: Unverified encryption may expose match composition between lobby and game servers
claims.description: `flow:process:lobby>process:game-server>hand-over-match` carries match composition and player identifiers from `process:lobby` to `process:game-server`, but its `protocol` and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If this internal handoff lacks effective encryption, an attacker with a foothold on the production path can intercept player identifiers and match composition. The disclosed mapping can enable targeted harassment, match surveillance, and correlation of player activity with records later written by `process:game-server`. This is conditional on the unknown transport protection and does not claim that the internal flow is plaintext.

quotes.text: The lobby reads the player database to set up a match, and hands the match over to the game servers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker needs a production-network observation position and encryption on this flow is only unknown. Impact is medium because the handoff carries player identifiers and match composition to `process:game-server`, which handles `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the lobby-to-server handoff
mitigations.detail: Define a TLS or mTLS protocol for `flow:process:lobby>process:game-server>hand-over-match`, record the resulting `protocol` and `encryption_in_transit`, and verify service identities.

claims.title: Player account records may be observable between the lobby and player database
claims.description: `flow:process:lobby>store:player-database>read-players` reads player account records from `store:player-database`, which is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If this database read path is not encrypted, a production-network observer can intercept player account records as the lobby forms matches. The records can then be correlated with match assignments and used to target specific players or support further account-focused attacks. This is a conditional transport-disclosure threat; the unknown attribute does not establish plaintext.

quotes.text: The lobby reads the player database to set up a match

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because observing this intra-production path requires a prior network foothold and its encryption state is unverified. Impact is high because the flow reads corpus-scale player account records from `store:player-database`, tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the lobby database read path
mitigations.detail: Use TLS with verified database and client identities on `flow:process:lobby>store:player-database>read-players`, including certificate validation on both ends.

mitigations.summary: Reduce read exposure
mitigations.detail: Limit the lobby query to the minimum player fields needed for match formation and use a database principal scoped to those fields.

claims.title: Unverified encryption may expose match statistics between game servers and the stats database
claims.description: `flow:process:game-server>store:stats-database>read-write-stats` carries match statistics to `store:stats-database`, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If protection on this production-network database path is absent or ineffective, an on-path attacker can intercept match statistics during reads or writes. The captured data can reveal player and match behavior and can support profiling or targeted exploitation of game activity. This draft is conditional on the unverified transport setting and does not assert that the database traffic is cleartext.

quotes.text: The game servers read and write the stats database during and after a match

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because interception requires a production-network position and `encryption_in_transit` is unverified. Impact is medium because `store:stats-database` holds `business-critical-data` covering match statistics.

mitigations.summary: Require encrypted database connections
mitigations.detail: Configure TLS for `flow:process:game-server>store:stats-database>read-write-stats` and require the game-server identity to validate the database certificate.

claims.title: Player progression and match results may be observable en route to the player database
claims.description: `flow:process:game-server>store:player-database>update-players` writes player progression and match results to `store:player-database`, which holds `pii` and `business-critical-data`; its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the database connection is not confidential, a production-network observer can intercept player-linked progression and match-result updates. Captured identifiers and outcomes can be correlated with the lobby's player-account reads, increasing the value of later account-targeted attacks. This threat remains conditional on the unknown encryption control.

quotes.text: they also write back to the player database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the attacker needs a production-network observation point and transport encryption is unverified. Impact is high because the path carries player-linked updates into `store:player-database`, which is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt game-server writes to player records
mitigations.detail: Require TLS or mTLS for `flow:process:game-server>store:player-database>update-players`, with certificate validation and a distinct least-privileged game-server database identity.

claims.title: Support-account moderation traffic may expose player data across the corporate boundary
claims.description: `flow:entity:customer-support-staff>process:moderation-website>moderate-accounts` crosses from `boundary:corporate-network` into `boundary:production-network` and carries moderation actions on player accounts, but `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. The production placement of `process:moderation-website` is inferred in the model, so the boundary premise should also be confirmed. If encryption is absent or ineffective, an attacker observing the corporate-to-production path can intercept player-related moderation requests and responses, exposing PII handled by `process:moderation-website`. The information can enable targeted account attacks or disclosure of moderation activity. This is conditional on the unknown transport control.

quotes.text: our customer support staff work from the corporate network and use a moderation website to look at and act on player accounts.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the flow crosses the corporate-to-production boundary and has unverified encryption, although the moderation website's production placement was inferred. Impact is medium because `process:moderation-website` handles `pii` in player-account moderation activity.

mitigations.summary: Require HTTPS or mTLS for staff moderation access
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:entity:customer-support-staff>process:moderation-website>moderate-accounts` to verified TLS, require strong staff authentication, and confirm the moderation website's actual trust-zone placement.

mitigations.summary: Minimize sensitive content in moderation responses
mitigations.detail: Return only the player-account fields necessary for the staff action and avoid exposing sensitive data in URLs or diagnostic responses.

claims.title: Player records may be observable between the moderation website and player database
claims.description: `flow:process:moderation-website>store:player-database>read-write-players` directly reads and writes player account records, while its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If this internal database path lacks effective encryption, an attacker observing the production path can intercept player account records and moderation state. The disclosure reaches beyond one staff action because the moderation website has a direct read path to `store:player-database`; captured records can be used to identify or target additional players. This is conditional on the unverified encryption state rather than a claim that the path is plaintext.

quotes.text: That website reads and writes the player database directly.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because an attacker needs a production-network observation position and encryption on the database flow is unknown. Impact is high because the directly accessed `store:player-database` contains `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt moderation database traffic
mitigations.detail: Require TLS or mTLS with verified service and database identities for `flow:process:moderation-website>store:player-database>read-write-players`.

mitigations.summary: Constrain the moderation read scope
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated database principal and views or row- and column-level controls that expose only records and fields required for support work.

claims.title: A copied player database may disclose player records if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:player-database` holds `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If that unknown resolves to no effective encryption at rest, an attacker who obtains a storage-layer copy, such as decommissioned media, a snapshot, or an operational backup of this store, can read player accounts directly without using the lobby or moderation access paths. The disclosure is corpus-scale and can be correlated with match assignments and progression data through the store's connected flows. This draft is conditional on the unverified at-rest protection and does not assert that encryption is absent.

quotes.text: The diagram doesn't record what authentication is on any of these links, or how any of the stores are protected.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the at-rest control is unverified and storage copies can be accessed outside the application path. Impact is high because `store:player-database` contains corpus-scale `pii` and `business-critical-data`, and copied-data disclosure is irreversible.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for player records
mitigations.detail: Establish the actual `encryption_at_rest` state for `store:player-database`, then require managed-key or customer-managed-key encryption for the primary store and every backup, snapshot, replica, and decommissioned volume.

mitigations.summary: Restrict storage-copy and key access
mitigations.detail: Separate storage export permissions from application access, limit decrypt permissions, and log and alert on backup or snapshot export operations.

claims.title: A copied stats database may disclose match statistics if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:stats-database` holds `business-critical-data`, while `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If the store or its operational copies are unencrypted, an attacker holding a disk, backup, snapshot, or other storage-layer copy can read match statistics without authenticating to `process:game-server`. The resulting corpus of match activity can be used for player profiling or to derive game-operational intelligence. This is conditional on the unknown encryption attribute and is not an assertion that the stats database is unencrypted.

quotes.text: The diagram doesn't record what authentication is on any of these links, or how any of the stores are protected.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because encryption at rest is unverified and storage copies bypass the live application access path. Impact is medium because `store:stats-database` contains business-critical match statistics, but no PII or credential asset is stated for that store.

mitigations.summary: Verify and encrypt stats-data copies
mitigations.detail: Determine the `encryption_at_rest` state for `store:stats-database` and enforce managed-key encryption for the primary store, backups, snapshots, and replicas.

mitigations.summary: Limit export and recovery access
mitigations.detail: Use separate, least-privileged principals for backup, restore, and export functions, and audit access to storage copies.

claims.title: Compromise of an existing player-database reader can disclose player records in bulk
claims.description: `process:lobby` reads `store:player-database` through `flow:process:lobby>store:player-database>read-players`, and `process:moderation-website` reads the same store through `flow:process:moderation-website>store:player-database>read-write-players`. An attacker executing code in either reader can use its existing read path to read player account records, including `pii` and `business-critical-data`; the model does not state authentication controls on either database flow. `process:lobby` is player-facing according to the source, making its inherited database reach especially important. Second-order, corpus access reveals player identity and account data that can be correlated with the lobby's matchmaking activity and used for targeted account attacks. This needs confirmation of the database identities, grants, field scope, and object-level authorization; it does not claim that either reader is already compromised or over-privileged.

quotes.text: Both of those have to be reachable from wherever a player is, so they are exposed.
That website reads and writes the player database directly.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because `process:lobby` is reachable by players and both database-flow authentication controls are unverified, although code execution in a reader remains a prerequisite. Impact is high because either existing reader can reach `store:player-database`, which holds `pii` and `business-critical-data` for player accounts.

mitigations.summary: Use separate least-privileged database identities
mitigations.detail: Give `process:lobby` and `process:moderation-website` distinct authenticated identities, each restricted to the rows, columns, and operations required for its task.

mitigations.summary: Enforce object-level authorization at the read path
mitigations.detail: Apply server-side ownership and support-scope checks for player-record retrieval, and do not rely on a compromised reader process to filter records correctly.

mitigations.summary: Constrain exposed reader reach
mitigations.detail: Segment database access so the player-facing lobby can reach only its required read interface and monitor anomalous bulk reads.

claims.title: Compromise of a game server can expose match statistics through its existing database access
claims.description: `process:game-server` reads and writes `store:stats-database` through `flow:process:game-server>store:stats-database>read-write-stats`, whose `authentication` is unknown. If an attacker executes code in a game server, it can use the server's existing database reach to read match statistics from `store:stats-database`. The game servers are reachable from arbitrary player networks according to the source, so this downstream access expands the consequence of a server compromise; disclosed statistics can support player profiling and reveal game-operation data. This draft is about the data the existing reader can disclose, not a claim that a compromise exists or that the unknown authentication control is absent.

quotes.text: Both of those have to be reachable from wherever a player is, so they are exposed.
The game servers read and write the stats database during and after a match

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because `process:game-server` is exposed to player networks and the authentication on its stats-database flow is unverified, though code execution on the server is still required. Impact is medium because `store:stats-database` is tagged `business-critical-data` and contains match statistics.

mitigations.summary: Scope game-server database access narrowly
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated authenticated identity for `process:game-server`, limited to required match-statistic partitions, operations, and fields.

mitigations.summary: Reduce the impact of a server foothold
mitigations.detail: Restrict game-server egress to the specific stats-database endpoint, use short-lived workload credentials, and alert on reads inconsistent with normal match processing.
